notes.kwanjula: When a bride introduces her groom to her family.

guidebook.intro: Ganda celebrations are big, colourful and long. The kwanjula, where a couple is introduced to the bride’s family, is one of the most important.

tips.title: The kwanjula
body: At a **kwanjula**, the groom’s family visits the bride’s home with many gifts. A spokesperson speaks for each side, and the bride’s **ssenga** (paternal aunt) plays a central role, guiding her and presenting the groom.
Women wear **gomesi** and men **kanzu** (Unit 10). The day ends with food, music and dancing.

tips.title: Wishing well
body: **Nkwagaliza** means “I wish you”: add what you wish: **Nkwagaliza amazaalibwa amalungi** (a good birthday). To a group, say **Mbaagaliza**. **Kulika** congratulates someone on something done: a wedding, a new baby, a journey.

culture.title: Everyone contributes
body: Weddings are often paid for together: friends and relatives hold planning meetings and pledge money. Being invited to a meeting means you are close to the family.
